kenneth-ken-petersen.text: Voted yes (April 1, 2025) on Resolution SCV-469, adopting retail water rate increases for FY 2025/26 through 2029/30; passed with Director Armitage the only no.

source.title: SCV Water Board approved minutes, April 1, 2025 (Resolution SCV-469 roll call)

kenneth-ken-petersen.text: (2023) Voted no on Ordinance No. 03 raising directors' per-meeting compensation 6.7%, from $239 to $255; it passed anyway.

source.title: SCV Water Board approved minutes, Dec. 19, 2023 (Ordinance No. 03 roll call)

kenneth-ken-petersen.text: Campaign site says he made the June 2025 motion authorizing a State Water Board financing agreement for the T and U Wells PFAS treatment project, and voted in Aug. 2025 to approve construction of the S Wells PFAS treatment facility.

source.title: Ken Petersen for Water Board 2026: Water Quality

kenneth-ken-petersen.text: Supports a water strategy including local groundwater, imported water and storage, "expanded recycled-water use," conservation, and the Pinetree Groundwater Recharge Project.

source.title: Ken Petersen for Water Board 2026: Water Supply

kenneth-ken-petersen.text: Lists "Financial Resiliency and Rate Changes" as a top issue: "keeping water rates affordable for residents and businesses is a delicate balance."

source.title: Ken Petersen for Water Board 2026: Top Issues

maria-a-gutzeit.text: As board president, voted yes (April 1, 2025) on Resolution SCV-469, adopting retail water rate increases for FY 2025/26 through 2029/30; passed with Director Armitage the only no.

source.title: SCV Water Board approved minutes, April 1, 2025 (Resolution SCV-469 roll call)

maria-a-gutzeit.text: (2023) Voted yes on Ordinance No. 03 raising directors' per-meeting compensation 6.7%, from $239 to $255.

source.title: SCV Water Board approved minutes, Dec. 19, 2023 (Ordinance No. 03 roll call)

maria-a-gutzeit.text: Survey priorities: "Safe, reliable water at the lowest possible cost"; plan proactively so the valley isn't hurt "by droughts and climate swings"; address new mandates efficiently. Lists "Government efficiency and transparency" as her passion.

source.title: Ballotpedia: Maria Gutzeit (2026 Candidate Connection survey)

maria-a-gutzeit.text: "Incentives, Not Fines": says she championed rebates and smart meters instead of penalizing customers to meet new state conservation targets.

source.title: Maria Gutzeit for SCV Water (campaign site)

maria-a-gutzeit.text: Says SCV Water under her watch secured millions in penalties from polluters for historic contamination, and that she pushed for extra groundwater monitoring near the closed Chiquita Canyon Landfill before regulators required it.

source.title: Maria Gutzeit for SCV Water (campaign site)

maria-a-gutzeit.text: Endorsed by LA County Supervisor Kathryn Barger, retired State Sen. Scott Wilk, and SCV Water directors Bill Cooper and Ken Petersen.

source.title: Maria Gutzeit for SCV Water (campaign site)

lynne-plambeck.text: "Water availability letters for thousands of unbuilt housing units should not be promised to developers while residents are told to cut back."

source.title: Ballotpedia: Lynne Plambeck (quoting campaign website, Sept. 24, 2026)

lynne-plambeck.text: Says reduced supply from climate change must be factored into planning so supplies "are not exaggerated," and polluted water should not count toward drinking-water supply until treatment is running.

source.title: Ballotpedia: Lynne Plambeck (quoting campaign website, Sept. 24, 2026)

lynne-plambeck.text: Campaign site: "Lynne voted against water rate increases and raising board member stipends," and calls the $73.8 million Valencia Water Co. purchase tied to Newhall Ranch water promises a "backroom deal."

source.title: Ballotpedia: Lynne Plambeck (quoting campaign website, Sept. 24, 2026)

lynne-plambeck.text: Pledges not to accept campaign contributions "from developers or their consultants, engineering firms related to development in our valley, construction companies or their attorneys."

Lists herself as executive director/president of the Santa Clarita Organization for Planning and the Environment and a former multi-term board member of the Sierra Club's Angeles Chapter; says "We must address climate change and drought in our water planning."
Endorsed by the LA County Democratic Party, Rep. George Whitesides, and Assemblywoman Pilar Schiavo.

notes: Two seats. Petersen and Gutzeit: roll-call votes from SCV Water's approved minutes (Apr. 1, 2025 rates; Dec. 19, 2023 stipends) plus campaign sites/survey. Plambeck (former director, left 2022): campaign site and endorsements; her claimed past votes against rate and stipend increases are her own statement, not checked against minutes. Petersen has no Ballotpedia survey. Searches used: 9
